Theme

Work & responsibility

shift noun

a turn of work

also work shift, night shift, day shift, in shifts, work in shifts, shift work, rota

classical

Caes. BG 7.85.5; 4.1.5 (Lewis & Short, s.v. invicem)

vicis, vicem, vice; pl. vicēs, vicibus f.

noun, third declension, no nominative singular

a turn; one’s turn in a succession

Change, succession, one’s turn (Lewis & Short); a shift is said through the turns: in vicem or per vicēs labōrāre, to work in shifts. The accusative vicem with a genitive or a possessive also means “instead of” or “on account of” (erī vicem meamque, Plaut. Capt. 3.3.11, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • in vicem (invicem) — in shifts, by turns

    adverb · also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.85.5: dēfatīgātīs in vicem integrī succēdunt (Lewis & Short)

    Caesar’s word for troops relieving each other; not in Cicero, who says vicissim (Lewis & Short). See in turn.

  • vigilia, vigiliae f. — a night watch

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.93: noctū vigiliās agere ad aedēs sacrās (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    One of the four watches into which the Romans divided the night, and the men who kept it: for a night shift of guards or nurses. Tertiā vigiliā, in the third watch, after midnight.

Examples

  • dēfatīgātīs in vicem integrī succēdunt

    fresh men take over from the tired, shift by shiftCaes. BG 7.85.5 (Lewis & Short)

  • hī rursus in vicem annō post in armīs sunt, illī domī remanent

    these in their turn are under arms the year after, and the others stay at homeCaes. BG 4.1.5 (Lewis & Short)

See also take turns, in turn, workman, employee.
